functions.name: DrainTwoListsWithMutexCleanup_B
functions.summary: Drains two queues guarded by a mutex. First, repeatedly pops queued items via sub_584E30 and dispatches each through the object's vtable method at offset 0x5C (thiscall(this, item)). Then, if the mutex handle at this+0x58C is non-null and WaitForSingleObject(this+0x58C, this+0x590) returns 0 (WAIT_OBJECT_0) or 128 (WAIT_ABANDONED), drains an embedded singly linked list control block at this+0x57C (head/tail/iterator/count): walks the list matching a node's data pointer, unlinks the node updating head/tail/iterator/count, runs SEH-guarded cleanup (0x005867B0) on flagged node payloads, and frees payload and node via FreeWrapper_7bcf. Finally releases the mutex (ReleaseMutex) when the handle is non-null. Called from AudioStreamingThreadShutdown (0x0057FDE0).

operations.description: First drain loop: while sub_584E30(this, &v11) returns nonzero, a queued item is popped into v11; the loop terminates when the first queue is empty.
Dispatch each popped item: virtual call at this->vtable[23] (offset 0x5C, +92) invoked as thiscall(this, v11).
Acquire the second-list mutex: WaitForSingleObject(handle at this+0x58C, timeout at this+0x590).

Second-list access guard: when the mutex handle is non-null and the wait result equals 0 (WAIT_OBJECT_0) or 128 (WAIT_ABANDONED), v5 is set to this+0x57C (the list control block); otherwise v5=0 and the second drain is skipped.
Second-list drain loop condition: node count at this+0x588 (equivalently *(this+0x57C)+0xC) is greater than 0.

Walk the embedded list from head (*v5) following each node's next pointer (node[1]), comparing each node's data pointer (*node) against the first node's data (v7); v8 tracks the previous node. Falling off the end of the list restarts the count check (LABEL_8).

Unlink the located node: if the iterator v5[2] points at it, advance it to the node's next; splice the previous node's next (or the head *v5) past the removed node; if the removed node was the tail v5[1], set the tail to the previous node. These writes correspond to the list control fields at this+0x57C/0x580/0x584 (and their *(this+0x57C)+0x0/0x4/0x8 aliases).
Decrement the node count (this+0x588, equivalently *(this+0x57C)+0xC).
If the node's flag byte (node+8) is set and the node's data pointer (*node) is non-null, run SEHGuardedFunctionWithExceptionHandling (0x005867B0) on the payload under an exception guard.
FreeWrapper_7bcf (0x00587BCF) releases the node's data payload when it was non-null.
FreeWrapper_7bcf (0x00587BCF) releases the unlinked node itself.
Return path: re-read the mutex handle at this+0x58C; when non-null, call ReleaseMutex on it and return its result; otherwise return 0.

functions.summary: Sets or clears bit a2 (bit index) in the byte array whose base pointer is stored at this[0]. a3 selects the action: nonzero sets the bit, zero clears it. Returns the resulting mask byte.

functions.name: AllocaStackProbe
functions.summary: MSVC CRT stack probe (_alloca_probe). Walks the stack pointer downward in 4096-byte strides while the requested allocation size a1 is at least 0x1000, touching each intervening page so the OS guard pages fire for large stack-frame growth. Returns via the bare retn that the original alloca call pushed, so it restores control directly to the caller of the prologue sequence. Per-iteration probe: decrement the pointer i by 4096 and reduce a1 by 4096, so each 4096-byte segment of the growing frame is visited exactly once.
Bare retn: returns to the address pushed by the alloca call site rather than a C-level return; no value is returned in the usual sense.
